why: The printed working sets a MINUS sign where a multiplication sign belongs, in all three lines that carry the numerator. Read literally, 2.315 g - 78 g/mol is -75.685 and cannot produce the book's own answer of 58.96; the value 58.96 follows only from 2.315 x 78 x 640 / (40 x 49). Occurrence 1 of 3.
solution: [Textbook misprint: the printed working sets a MINUS sign where a multiplication sign belongs, writing "2.315 g - 78 g/mol" in all three lines that carry the numerator. Read literally that is \(-75.685\) and cannot produce the book's own answer; 58.96 follows only from \(2.315 \times 78 \times 640/(40 \times 49)\). The operator has been corrected below, and the final unit, printed as "g mol", restored to \(\mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}\). The answer 58.96 \(\mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}\) is correct.]
